metadata.architecture: scalar sinusoidal causal attention without a direct token shortcut
metadata.author: declarative architecture search
metadata.mechanism_hypothesis: Removing the direct positioned-token shortcut will force tied readout logits to depend entirely on causal attention, preventing local token identity from overwhelming contextual digit and carry information without adding parameters.
metadata.name: Scalar Pure Context Attention Addition Model
metadata.research_current_explanation: The 19-parameter fixed context-emphasizing mixture still scores 0.000000, indicating that retaining even a downweighted direct positioned-token path did not yield measurable accuracy.
metadata.research_decision_rule: Accept only if the graph is valid, preserves the frozen public eligibility floor, and either has fewer than 19 trusted parameters or improves public accuracy at exactly 19 parameters.
metadata.research_evidence: The current result shows no public improvement from mixing the positioned-token shortcut at weight 0.25 with the causal-attention output at weight 1.0.
metadata.research_expected_result: Pure contextual readout should retain the 19-parameter count and improve public accuracy if shortcut interference was suppressing the attention-derived carry signal.
metadata.research_next_experiment: Remove the fixed routing node and connect causal attention directly to the tied readout, forcing all logits to use contextualized representations.
metadata.research_previous_interpretation: The context-emphasizing fixed mixture remained at 0.000000, so partial shortcut suppression was insufficient and motivates complete shortcut removal.
